metric: Translations from SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL into six databases' dialects, proved equal to the source in the source's dialect after sqlglot reads both; parsed means both sides parse in their own dialect.
correctness: Every BIRDTrans proof is re-run on 300 random SQLite databases (DuckDB translations also natively in DuckDB); 492 pairs where the two databases read the same text differently (LIKE case, string collations, integer and decimal division, Unix time ranges, row values, SQLite type conversion; the docs list every rule) are left unproved, and so are 12 that call the clock, a random value, a sequence or the session. With DLBENCH_NATIVE set, this run also replayed 138 of the 163 proofs on the databases themselves (mysql>clickhouse 11, mysql>duckdb 10, mysql>mariadb 29, mysql>postgresql 14, sqlite>clickhouse 19, sqlite>duckdb 26, sqlite>postgresql 29; clickhouse 26.9.2.1, duckdb 1.5.6, mariadb 10.11.14, mysql 8.0.46, postgresql 16.15, sqlite 3.53.1): 0 differences. Not replayed: 10 no MonetDB engine, 9 not a query, 6 not replayable. 2/203 'approximate' pairs are proved (listed in the docs). 10 of the exact proofs are a MariaDB translation that is its MySQL source token for token, where the provers have nothing to read (an INSERT, a table with no published definition); statements whose answer can change between two runs are refused.
caveats: Pinned subset of the 6,402 pairs (every approximate pair, one in ten of the rest); run --data with a DLBench checkout for all. Labels are LLM plus human review, not proofs. Proofs are about sqlglot's reading of each dialect; MariaDB is read as MySQL and MonetDB as PostgreSQL. The 32-bit float, division-by-zero, decimal and ClickHouse rules were added after a first run on the whole subset showed two proofs contradicted natively in DuckDB (tuned on test). The 2026-11-11 harness changes (translated column and table spellings read back, the same-statement rule, the volatile-call refusal, and the gap rules that the native replay of every proof led to) were developed on the development split only; held-out pairs were replayed for their verdicts, never read.
